newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Sterling seen capped around 3.0360 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Sterling seen capped around 3.0360 marks.

text.p: Sterling's push above 3.03 marks in early European trade has set the stage for further gains but chartists see the pair well capped around 3.0360 marks.
For a volatile sterling, which sank to lows of 2.9735 this week, a vault above 3.0360 marks, the high on July 28, means it could push towards 3.06 highs again, said chartists.
"On the hourly charts it is rising in a channel range at the moment...But the top side is quite limited," said Nick Shamin, technical analyst at ANZ Investment.
At 0740 GMT sterling/mark stood at 3.0303/08 against 3.0130/40 in late Europe on Thursday.
Above 3.0360 marks, chartists said sterling/mark would be capped around 3.0460 marks. "This represents hourly lows seen between 24 and 28 of July," said ANZ's Shamin.
Analysts said sterling/mark, well supported by a short-term trendline, also gained ground in Europe as it was propelled by a powering dollar/mark.
ANZ's Shamin said the five-day moving average of around 2.9 marks is also providing support as it tweaks higher.
Chartists said a short-term trendline, dating back to July 29 lows of 2.9735 marks and cutting in around 3.0020 marks, should provide a good floor.
On a break, sterling/mark should remain constructive as long as it manages to hold above support at 2.9840/60 and 2.9800 marks.
Below that, analysts said a long-term upward trendline, dating from around July 1996 and cutting in around 2.8400 marks, would provide a solid floor.
For cable, which sank to its lowest in more than seven weeks to $1.6203 on Wednesday but managed to hold its ground above $1.64 on Thursday, chartists said the bias was to the upside.
At 0915 GMT, cable was trading at $1.6398/08 against $1.6404/14 in late Europe.
